output.question: Who owns Xfinity?
output.answer: Comcast Corporation (Nasdaq: CMCSA), headquartered in Philadelphia, owns Xfinity. It is Comcast's consumer brand for broadband, WiFi, mobile, video and home security. On June 29, 2026, Comcast announced a plan to split into two public companies by spinning off NBCUniversal and Sky in a tax-free transaction. Xfinity and the internet business stay with Comcast, so the split does not change who owns Xfinity. The spin-off is expected to take about a year, and reports say former CFO Michael Angelakis will become CEO of the remaining Comcast broadband company.

key_facts.fact: Xfinity is a Comcast brand. A June 2026 Comcast release refers to 'Comcast's Xfinity', and an executive's title is 'SVP & GM Connectivity at Comcast's Xfinity'.
Comcast's own boilerplate says it delivers broadband, wireless and video through Xfinity, Comcast Business and Sky. This text appeared only in a search-result snippet; the page did not load.

Comcast plans to spin off NBCUniversal and Sky into a separate public company. Comcast, based in Philadelphia, keeps its residential and business internet services (Xfinity). Completion is expected in about a year, and Michael Angelakis is to become CEO of the broadband company.

caveats: The NBCUniversal/Sky spin-off had not finished as of the latest sources (June 2026; about a year expected, pending regulatory and board approvals). The details of the remaining Comcast company could still change.

The Angelakis CEO detail is a paraphrase of the AP article, not a direct quote.
Comcast is publicly traded. Search snippets say the Roberts family keeps voting control through dual-class shares, but no page I opened confirmed this.
